stem: A Massachusetts school of pharmacy launches a new clinical pharmacy program and tells students their participation will count toward the internship requirement. What does the regulation actually require before that credit is available?

choices.text: The school must submit a written program description and the Board determines creditability.
Nothing further, because clinical pharmacy is already a listed internship setting.
Each student must individually petition the Board for credit after completing the program.
The program must be separately accredited by ACPE before any credit is available.
The preceptor must certify the hours, after which internship credit follows automatically.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 8.01(12) requires Massachusetts approved colleges and schools of pharmacy to submit to the Board a written description of each demonstration project or clinical pharmacy program for which internship credit is desired, and the Board may determine whether student participation may be credited toward the internship requirement. The determination is the Board's, on the school's submission.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: the school submits a description and the Board determines creditability.
choice_analysis.B: Being a listed setting does not by itself make a particular program creditable.
choice_analysis.C: The submission duty sits on the school, not on each student.
choice_analysis.D: Separate ACPE accreditation of the program is not the stated mechanism.
choice_analysis.E: Preceptor certification does not replace the Board's determination.

related_facts: The Board issues a Summary of Objectives and Procedures for Pharmacy Internship and preceptor guidelines.
explanation.mpje_trap: A qualifying category is not the same as an approved program; the Board still decides.

reasoning_steps: Identify the new offering as a clinical pharmacy program seeking internship credit
Reserve the creditability decision to the Board
